verdicts.claim: From 1992 to 2018... Republicans gained vote share between the general election and the runoff in seven of eight statewide general-election runoffs (Inside Elections).
verdicts.evidence: Inside Elections (c. Nov 2020) covers eight statewide general/special runoffs since 1988 and says 'Democrats have won just one of them' (1998 PSC). Its figures show the GOP candidate's share rising in the other seven: Coverdell 47.7 to 50.7; Baker 48.3 to 56.8; Eaton 46.3 to 51.8; Chambliss 49.8 to 57; McDonald 47.2 to 57; Raffensperger 49.1 to 51.9; Eaton 49.7 to 51.8. In 1998 Cole fell from 42.1 to about 35. The share-gain wording is the page's own calculation from those figures, not the article's sentence. Part of the gain is mechanical, because third-party votes drop out; in 2018 the Democrat (Miller) also 'increased her vote share'.
verdicts.fix: Optional, more precise: 'Republicans won seven of the eight statewide general-election runoffs from 1992 to 2018 (Inside Elections).'

flags: GATE: gate.py K8 reads only the 'verdicts' array. Earlier verdict files (e.g. the-promise-audit) put page-held claims under 'script_held', which the gate ignores. Here every page claim is in 'verdicts' (ids p01-p49) so that it is gated.

LEDGER: the extractor caught 1 claim (c001, the EP 09 crumb). The page's own tags (FACT/INFERENCE spans, tier labels, Documented/Illustrative) are not extracted. The other 49 items were checked by reading the page and its script.

WITHDRAWN CLAIM PERSISTS OFF-PAGE: episode-04-the-influence-war.html:3059 ('down-ballot anomalies as the surface trace of an influence operation'); claims-atlas.html:~505 (an atlas entry for this page still asserting the targeting claim; ~500 asserts 'documented demographic skew' that this page now says it did not measure); episode-08-the-class-engine.html:2415 ('this is the cohort EP 04 documented'); episode-09-the-synthetic-self.html:581 ('where between election targeting lives'); episode-07-the-physical-plant.html:3881 (an unverified PSC 'runoff cohort' claim). Not edited; for the editor.

FRAME: the EP 09 crumb ('Between elections is where a synthetic voice would be deployed first and seen last') brings the withdrawn 'between elections' targeting frame back onto this page. It has no connection to the Georgia runoffs.

FRAME (other side): FairVote is a ranked-choice advocacy group, and the page never says so. The method note's counter-argument is present, so the Editorial Standard's other-side requirement is met in form. No Anthropic conflict note is needed; AI is not a subject.

FRAME: the race-card characterizations are the page's own and unsourced: 'chamber-aligned GOP vs conservative-movement wing', 'election-administration credibility vs insurgent media presence' (Fleming is a state representative), 'legal-credentials lane vs media-fluency lane' (Barrett is a sitting Fulton County commissioner). Not graded as fact.

FRAME: lens C's slope chart draws exact 'Primary ad mentions / Runoff ad mentions' values and lens D's compass prints 'mismatch/aligned' per race, with no 'illustrative' label on either chart. The discipline section discloses it, but a reader of the chart alone will not see that.

STALE: the hero canvas still prints 'today' at day 3; the sources header says 'verified May 22, 2026' but includes entries added Nov. 11; 'Georgia is about to tell on itself' and 'The shape of June 16 is set' keep pre-vote tense with no 'as drafted' cue. The status box omits November outcomes that bear on it: Bottoms beat Jackson; Kingston won GA-01 (WTOC, Nov 4-5).
REASONING: the method note says 'a repeat of the 2021 inversion' would change our mind, yet the page says 2022 'held the reversal'. By its own account the condition was already met.
SOURCE LABEL: MIT/MEDSL is tiered 'T2 · peer-reviewed analysis', but the report (Hood & McKee) does not describe itself as peer-reviewed and covers general-election runoffs only.

COULD NOT OPEN: WABE 'What's settled and unsettled' (site error); sos.ga.gov results and calendar (proxy refused; used the Gordon County reproduction); FiveThirtyEight, Georgia Recorder May 19 link, NPR results app, Ballotpedia GA 2026 (proxy refused). The claims they back were checked through other sources where possible.
No source contained text addressed to an AI or a reviewer.
